questions.question: What is the remainder when $P(x)=x^3-2x^2+x+5$ is divided by $(x-2)$?
questions.answer: By the remainder theorem, $P(2)=8-8+2+5=7$ (C).

questions.question: A particle has four ropes attached to it. The ropes pull the particle with forces $\mathbf i+4\mathbf j$, $b\mathbf i-3\mathbf j$, $8\mathbf i$ and $a\mathbf j$ as shown in the diagram. If the particle is in equilibrium, what are the values of $a$ and $b$?
questions.answer: In equilibrium the resultant is zero. $\mathbf i$: $1+b+8=0\Rightarrow b=-9$. $\mathbf j$: $4-3+a=0\Rightarrow a=-1$ (C).

questions.question: What is the range of $y=\pi+\tan^{-1}(x)$?
questions.answer: $\tan^{-1}x\in\left(-\frac\pi2,\frac\pi2\right)$, so adding $\pi$ gives $y\in\left(\frac\pi2,\frac{3\pi}2\right)$ (B).

questions.question: How many arrangements in a row of the letters of the word SECRETS begin and end with E?
questions.answer: Fix an E at each end (there are two Es, so they are used up). The remaining letters S, C, R, T, S are arranged in the middle: $\dfrac{5!}{2!}$ (D), as the two Ss are identical.

questions.question: The surface area of a sphere is increasing at a rate of $0.05\ \text{mm}^2/\text{s}$. At what rate is the radius changing when it is $4$ mm?
questions.answer: $S=4\pi r^2\Rightarrow\dfrac{dS}{dr}=8\pi r$. $\dfrac{dr}{dt}=\dfrac{dS/dt}{dS/dr}=\dfrac{0.05}{8\pi(4)}=\dfrac{1}{640\pi}$ mm/s (B).

questions.question: What is the magnitude of the projection of $\mathbf u=\begin{pmatrix}5\\-1\end{pmatrix}$ onto $\mathbf v=\begin{pmatrix}2\\9\end{pmatrix}$?
questions.answer: $|\operatorname{proj}_{\mathbf v}\mathbf u|=\dfrac{|\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf v|}{|\mathbf v|}=\dfrac{|10-9|}{\sqrt{4+81}}=\dfrac1{\sqrt{85}}$ (A).

questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to $\displaystyle\int\frac1{\sqrt{7-4x^2}}\,dx$?
questions.answer: $\displaystyle\int\frac{dx}{\sqrt{7-(2x)^2}}=\frac12\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{2x}{\sqrt7}\right)+C$ (A).

questions.question: When expanded, which expression contains a non-zero constant term?
questions.answer: In $\left(x^2-x^{-1/2}\right)^n$ the general term is $\binom nk(x^2)^{n-k}\left(-x^{-1/2}\right)^k$, with power of $x$: $2(n-k)-\frac k2=2n-\frac{5k}2$. For a constant term, $k=\frac{4n}5$ must be an integer, so $5\mid n$. Only $n=10$ qualifies ($k=8$) (D).

questions.question: Two particles move simultaneously along the curves $y=f(x)$ (starting from $A$) and $y=f^{-1}(x)$ (starting from $B$) respectively, as shown. When the particle on $y=f(x)$ reaches $P$, it is one unit vertically above the origin. At that moment, the particle on $y=f^{-1}(x)$ reaches point $Q$ and is one unit to the right of the origin. The velocity vector of the particle at $Q$ is $\begin{pmatrix}\sqrt3\\1\end{pmatrix}$. Which of the following could represent the velocity vector at $P$?
questions.answer: The graph of $y=f^{-1}(x)$ is the reflection of $y=f(x)$ in $y=x$, and $Q$ is the reflection of $P$. The particles move simultaneously, so the motion of one is the reflection of the other, and reflecting in $y=x$ swaps the components of a vector. The velocity at $P$ is therefore $\begin{pmatrix}1\\\sqrt3\end{pmatrix}$ (B).

questions.question: Solve $\dfrac{4x}{2-x}\ge3$.
questions.answer:
$x\ne2$. $\dfrac{4x}{2-x}-3\ge0\Rightarrow\dfrac{7x-6}{2-x}\ge0$. Multiply by $(2-x)^2>0$: $(7x-6)(2-x)\ge0$, so $\dfrac67\le x<2$ (excluding $x=2$).
$$\frac67\le x<2$$

questions.question: Find the derivative of $y=x\arctan(2x)$.
questions.answer: By the product rule, $y'=\arctan(2x)+x\cdot\dfrac{2}{1+4x^2}=\arctan(2x)+\dfrac{2x}{1+4x^2}$.

questions.question: The parametric equations of a curve are $x=e^{-4t}$ and $y=e^{12t}-1$. Find the Cartesian equation of this curve, stating any restrictions on the domain and range.
questions.answer: $e^{4t}=\dfrac1x$, so $e^{12t}=\dfrac1{x^3}$. Hence $$y=\frac1{x^3}-1.$$ Since $x=e^{-4t}>0$ and $y=e^{12t}-1>-1$: domain $x>0$, range $y>-1$.

questions.question: Two prefects sit around a circular table with six other students. Find the number of possible seating arrangements.
questions.answer: Eight people around a circle: $(8-1)!=7!=5040$.

questions.question: Two prefects sit around a circular table with six other students. Find the number of seating arrangements if the prefects are not seated together.
questions.answer: Prefects together: treat them as one block, giving $(7-1)!\times2!=6!\times2=1440$ arrangements. Not together: $5040-1440=3600$.

questions.question: Use the substitution $u=e^x+3$ to find $\displaystyle\int_0^{\ln6}\frac{e^x}{(e^x+3)^{3/2}}\,dx$.
questions.answer:
$du=e^x\,dx$; $x=0\Rightarrow u=4$, $x=\ln6\Rightarrow u=9$.
$\displaystyle\int_4^9u^{-3/2}\,du=\Big[-2u^{-1/2}\Big]_4^9=-2\left(\frac13-\frac12\right)=\frac13$.

questions.question: Using the substitution $t=\tan\theta$, solve $\sec2\theta-2\tan2\theta=1$ for $0\le\theta\le\pi$.
questions.answer:
With $t=\tan\theta$: $\cos2\theta=\dfrac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}$ and $\tan2\theta=\dfrac{2t}{1-t^2}$, so $\sec2\theta=\dfrac{1+t^2}{1-t^2}$ (for $t\ne\pm1$).
$\dfrac{1+t^2}{1-t^2}-\dfrac{4t}{1-t^2}=1\Rightarrow1+t^2-4t=1-t^2\Rightarrow2t^2-4t=0\Rightarrow t=0$ or $t=2$.
$\tan\theta=0\Rightarrow\theta=0,\pi$; $\tan\theta=2\Rightarrow\theta=\tan^{-1}2\approx1.107$.
$$\theta=0,\ 1.107,\ \pi$$ (check $\theta=\frac\pi2$, where $t$ is undefined: $\sec\pi-2\tan\pi=-1\ne1$, so it is not a solution).

questions.question: Evaluate $(\mathbf a+\mathbf b)\cdot\mathbf c$, given $\mathbf a=\begin{pmatrix}5\\-1\end{pmatrix}$, $\mathbf b=\begin{pmatrix}-4\\2\end{pmatrix}$ and $\mathbf c=\begin{pmatrix}3\\7\end{pmatrix}$.
questions.answer: $\mathbf a+\mathbf b=\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\end{pmatrix}$, so $(\mathbf a+\mathbf b)\cdot\mathbf c=3+7=10$.

questions.question: Using $(\mathbf a+\mathbf b)\cdot\mathbf c=10$ (with $\mathbf a+\mathbf b=\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\end{pmatrix}$ and $\mathbf c=\begin{pmatrix}3\\7\end{pmatrix}$), find the size of the acute angle between $\mathbf a+\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$. Give your answer to the nearest degree.
questions.answer: $\cos\theta=\dfrac{10}{\sqrt2\sqrt{58}}=\dfrac{10}{\sqrt{116}}\Rightarrow\theta=21.8^\circ\approx22^\circ$.

questions.question: Determine the coefficient of $x^2$ in the expansion of $(3-2x)(2+x)^4$.
questions.answer:
$(3-2x)(2+x)^4=3(2+x)^4-2x(2+x)^4$. Using $(2+x)^4=\sum\binom4k2^{4-k}x^k$:
the $x^2$ coefficient of $(2+x)^4$ is $\binom42\,2^2=24$, and the $x^1$ coefficient is $\binom41\,2^3=32$.
Coefficient of $x^2$ $=3(24)-2(32)=72-64=8$.

questions.question: Use mathematical induction to prove that, for integers $n\ge1$, $$\ln\!\left(\frac1{1+2}\right)+\ln\!\left(\frac2{2+2}\right)+\ln\!\left(\frac3{3+2}\right)+\dots+\ln\!\left(\frac n{n+2}\right)=\ln\!\left(\frac2{(n+1)(n+2)}\right)$$
questions.answer:
**Base case** $n=1$: LHS $=\ln\frac13$; RHS $=\ln\frac{2}{2\cdot3}=\ln\frac13$. ✓
**Assume** the result holds for $n=k$ ($k\ge1$).
**Then** for $n=k+1$: LHS $=\ln\!\left(\dfrac{2}{(k+1)(k+2)}\right)+\ln\!\left(\dfrac{k+1}{k+3}\right)=\ln\!\left(\dfrac{2(k+1)}{(k+1)(k+2)(k+3)}\right)=\ln\!\left(\dfrac2{(k+2)(k+3)}\right)=\ln\!\left(\dfrac{2}{((k+1)+1)((k+1)+2)}\right)$ = RHS.
So it holds for $n=k+1$, and by induction for all integers $n\ge1$. $\blacksquare$

questions.question: An $11$-metre ladder rests with one end against a wall and the other end on horizontal ground, level with the base of the wall, $x$ metres from the bottom of the wall. The end on the ground is sliding away from the wall at a constant rate of $0.1$ m/s. Find the rate at which the angle $\theta$, in radians, between the ground and the ladder is decreasing when the ladder is $6$ metres away from the wall.
questions.answer:
$\cos\theta=\dfrac x{11}\Rightarrow x=11\cos\theta$, so $\dfrac{dx}{d\theta}=-11\sin\theta$ and $\dfrac{d\theta}{dx}=\dfrac{-1}{11\sin\theta}$.
$\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}=\dfrac{d\theta}{dx}\cdot\dfrac{dx}{dt}=\dfrac{-0.1}{11\sin\theta}$.
When $x=6$: $\cos\theta=\frac6{11}$, $\sin\theta=\frac{\sqrt{121-36}}{11}=\frac{\sqrt{85}}{11}$.
$\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}=\dfrac{-0.1}{\sqrt{85}}\approx-0.0108$. The angle is decreasing at $\dfrac{0.1}{\sqrt{85}}\approx0.0108$ rad/s.

questions.question: Show that $2\sin5x\cos x=\sin6x+\sin4x$.
questions.answer: $2\sin5x\cos x=2\cdot\tfrac12\left[\sin(5x+x)+\sin(5x-x)\right]=\sin6x+\sin4x$. $\blacksquare$

questions.question: Hence, find $\displaystyle\int\frac{\sin4x+\sin6x}{\cos4x+\cos6x}\,dx$.
questions.answer:
Using part (i), $\sin4x+\sin6x=2\sin5x\cos x$, and similarly $\cos6x+\cos4x=2\cos5x\cos x$. So
$\displaystyle\int\frac{2\sin5x\cos x}{2\cos5x\cos x}dx=\int\tan5x\,dx=-\frac15\ln|\cos5x|+c$.

questions.question: Write $\sqrt3\cos x+\sin x$ in the form $R\cos(x-\alpha)$, where $R>0$ and $0<\alpha<\dfrac\pi2$.
questions.answer:
$R\cos\alpha=\sqrt3$, $R\sin\alpha=1$. $R^2=3+1=4\Rightarrow R=2$; $\tan\alpha=\frac1{\sqrt3}\Rightarrow\alpha=\frac\pi6$.
$$\sqrt3\cos x+\sin x=2\cos\!\left(x-\frac\pi6\right)$$

questions.question: A region bounded by the curve $y=\sqrt3\cos x+\sin x+2$ and the coordinate axes is shown. The curve touches the $x$-axis at $x=\dfrac{7\pi}6$. Hence, or otherwise, find the volume of the solid formed when the shaded region is rotated about the $x$-axis.
questions.answer:
By part (i), $y=2\cos\!\left(x-\frac\pi6\right)+2$.
$V=\pi\displaystyle\int_0^{7\pi/6}\left[2\cos\!\left(x-\tfrac\pi6\right)+2\right]^2dx=4\pi\int_0^{7\pi/6}\left[\cos^2\!\left(x-\tfrac\pi6\right)+2\cos\!\left(x-\tfrac\pi6\right)+1\right]dx$
$=4\pi\displaystyle\int_0^{7\pi/6}\left[\tfrac32+\tfrac12\cos\!\left(2x-\tfrac\pi3\right)+2\cos\!\left(x-\tfrac\pi6\right)\right]dx=4\pi\left[\tfrac{3x}2+\tfrac14\sin\!\left(2x-\tfrac\pi3\right)+2\sin\!\left(x-\tfrac\pi6\right)\right]_0^{7\pi/6}$
Upper limit: $\frac{7\pi}4+\frac14\sin2\pi+2\sin\pi=\frac{7\pi}4$. Lower limit: $0+\frac14\sin\!\left(-\frac\pi3\right)+2\sin\!\left(-\frac\pi6\right)=-\frac{\sqrt3}8-1$.
$$V=4\pi\left(\frac{7\pi}4+\frac{\sqrt3}8+1\right)=7\pi^2+\frac{\sqrt3\,\pi}2+4\pi\ \text{units}^3$$

questions.question: Show that $\sec\!\left(2\sin^{-1}x\right)$ can be expressed as $\dfrac1{1-2x^2}$.
questions.answer: Let $\alpha=\sin^{-1}x$ (so $\sin\alpha=x$, $-1\le x\le1$). $\sec2\alpha=\dfrac1{\cos2\alpha}=\dfrac1{1-2\sin^2\alpha}=\dfrac1{1-2x^2}$. $\blacksquare$

questions.question: Hence, sketch the function $f(x)=\sec\!\left(2\sin^{-1}x\right)$.
questions.answer:
By part (i), $f(x)=\dfrac1{1-2x^2}$ on the domain $-1\le x\le1$, $x\ne\pm\frac1{\sqrt2}$.
- Vertical asymptotes at $x=\pm\frac1{\sqrt2}$.
- For $|x|<\frac1{\sqrt2}$: $f(x)\ge1$ with a minimum at $(0,1)$, rising to $+\infty$ at the asymptotes.
- For $\frac1{\sqrt2}<|x|\le1$: $f(x)\le-1$, coming from $-\infty$ at the asymptote to the endpoints $(\pm1,-1)$.

questions.question: The points $A$ and $B$ have position vectors $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ relative to a fixed point $O$. The vector $\overrightarrow{AB}$ is extended to a point $C$ such that $|\overrightarrow{AB}|:|\overrightarrow{AC}|=1:4$. The vector $\overrightarrow{OB}$ is extended to a point $D$ such that $|\overrightarrow{OB}|:|\overrightarrow{OD}|=1:k$, where $k$ is a positive constant. If $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{CD}$ are perpendicular, show that $k=\dfrac{3|\mathbf a|^2-7\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b+4|\mathbf b|^2}{|\mathbf b|^2-\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b}$.
questions.answer:
$\overrightarrow{AB}=\mathbf b-\mathbf a$, $\overrightarrow{AC}=4\overrightarrow{AB}=4\mathbf b-4\mathbf a$, $\overrightarrow{OD}=k\mathbf b$.
$\overrightarrow{OC}=\mathbf a+4\mathbf b-4\mathbf a=4\mathbf b-3\mathbf a$, so $\overrightarrow{CD}=k\mathbf b-(4\mathbf b-3\mathbf a)=3\mathbf a+(k-4)\mathbf b$.
$\overrightarrow{AB}\cdot\overrightarrow{CD}=0$: $[3\mathbf a+(k-4)\mathbf b]\cdot(\mathbf b-\mathbf a)=0$
$3\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b-3|\mathbf a|^2+(k-4)|\mathbf b|^2-(k-4)\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b=0$
$(k-4)\left(|\mathbf b|^2-\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b\right)=3|\mathbf a|^2-3\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b$
$k=4+\dfrac{3|\mathbf a|^2-3\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b}{|\mathbf b|^2-\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b}=\dfrac{4|\mathbf b|^2-4\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b+3|\mathbf a|^2-3\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b}{|\mathbf b|^2-\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b}=\dfrac{3|\mathbf a|^2-7\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b+4|\mathbf b|^2}{|\mathbf b|^2-\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b}$. $\blacksquare$

questions.question: A projectile is launched from the origin at ground level with an initial velocity of $V$ m/s at an angle $\theta$ above the horizontal. The displacement vector $t$ seconds after launch is $\mathbf r(t)=\begin{pmatrix}Vt\cos\theta\\-\frac12gt^2+Vt\sin\theta\end{pmatrix}$ (do not prove this). Show that the maximum height attained by the projectile is $\dfrac{V^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$.
questions.answer:
$\mathbf v(t)=\begin{pmatrix}V\cos\theta\\-gt+V\sin\theta\end{pmatrix}$. At maximum height $\dot y=0$: $t=\dfrac{V\sin\theta}g$.
$y_{\max}=-\frac12g\left(\frac{V\sin\theta}g\right)^2+V\sin\theta\cdot\frac{V\sin\theta}g=-\frac{V^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}+\frac{V^2\sin^2\theta}g=\dfrac{V^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$. $\blacksquare$

questions.question: A projectile is launched from the origin at ground level with initial speed $V$ at angle $\theta$ above the horizontal, with maximum height $\dfrac{V^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$. Hence, determine the set of values of $\theta$ for which the maximum height reached by the projectile is less than its range. Give your answer to the nearest degree.
questions.answer:
Range: $y=0\Rightarrow t\left(V\sin\theta-\frac12gt\right)=0$, so the time of flight is $t=\dfrac{2V\sin\theta}g$ and $R=V\cos\theta\cdot\dfrac{2V\sin\theta}g=\dfrac{2V^2\sin\theta\cos\theta}g$.
$y_{\max}<R$: $\dfrac{V^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}<\dfrac{2V^2\sin\theta\cos\theta}g\Rightarrow\sin^2\theta<4\sin\theta\cos\theta$.
For $0<\theta<\frac\pi2$, $\sin\theta>0$: $\sin\theta<4\cos\theta\Rightarrow\tan\theta<4\Rightarrow\theta<76^\circ$.
$$0^\circ<\theta<76^\circ$$

questions.question: The function $f(x)=\dfrac{1+kx}{x^2-1}$ is continuous in the domain $-1<x<1$. Find the values of $k$ such that the inverse function $f^{-1}(x)$ exists.
questions.answer:
$f^{-1}$ exists only if $f$ is one-to-one, i.e. monotonic on $(-1,1)$, so $f'(x)$ must not change sign.
$f'(x)=\dfrac{k(x^2-1)-2x(1+kx)}{(x^2-1)^2}=\dfrac{-(kx^2+2x+k)}{(x^2-1)^2}$. The sign of $f'$ is the sign of $-(kx^2+2x+k)$.
The quadratic $kx^2+2x+k$ keeps one sign for all $x$ if $k>0$ and $\Delta\le0$, or $k<0$ and $\Delta\le0$. $\Delta=4-4k^2\le0\Rightarrow k^2\ge1\Rightarrow k\le-1$ or $k\ge1$. (If $|k|<1$ the roots have product $1$, so exactly one lies in $(-1,1)$ and $f'$ changes sign; $k=0$ gives $f'\propto-2x$, which also changes sign.)
$$k\le-1\ \text{ or }\ k\ge1$$

questions.question: The equation $px^3+qx+r=0$ has a double root. Show that $27pr^2+4q^3=0$.
questions.answer:
Let $P(x)=px^3+qx+r$. A double root $\alpha$ satisfies $P(\alpha)=0$ and $P'(\alpha)=3p\alpha^2+q=0$, so $\alpha^2=-\dfrac q{3p}$.
$r=-p\alpha^3-q\alpha=-\alpha\left(p\alpha^2+q\right)=-\alpha\cdot\dfrac{2q}3$. Squaring: $r^2=\dfrac{4q^2}9\alpha^2=\dfrac{4q^2}9\cdot\left(-\dfrac q{3p}\right)=-\dfrac{4q^3}{27p}$.
$27pr^2=-4q^3\Rightarrow27pr^2+4q^3=0$. $\blacksquare$

questions.question: Using $27pr^2+4q^3=0$ for a cubic $px^3+qx+r=0$ with a double root, find the exact value of the $y$ coordinates of the stationary points on the curve $y=2x^3-3x-1$ without the use of calculus.
questions.answer:
A stationary point at height $y=k$ corresponds to $2x^3-3x-1=k$ having a double root, i.e. $2x^3-3x-(1+k)=0$. Here $p=2$, $q=-3$, $r=-(1+k)$.
$27(2)(1+k)^2+4(-27)=0\Rightarrow54(1+k)^2=108\Rightarrow(1+k)^2=2\Rightarrow k=-1\pm\sqrt2$.
The $y$ coordinates are $-1+\sqrt2$ and $-1-\sqrt2$.
